transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—thanks for coming today. To start, can you tell me what's been bothering you or what brought you in to see me?

Well, thank you. What finally made me make this appointment is... well, it happens when I'm driving. The moment my car reaches one of those long bridges, you know, the ones heading toward Miami... my chest just tightens up completely. My hands clamp down on the steering wheel, and I get this sudden certainty that I have to get off the bridge right that second. Even though, of course, there’s nowhere to go once you're up there. It's just become too much to deal with.
Does this intense fear and chest tightness happen only when you're on a bridge, or have you noticed it in other situations too, like tunnels, crowded places, or being far from home?

No, it's really just the bridges. I don't have any trouble with tunnels, and... well, crowded places or being far from home don't bother me at all. I've traveled plenty in my life without any issues. It really is just when I'm driving up onto a bridge that this happens.

The fear is confined to a single specific situational trigger (bridges) rather than recurrent unexpected panic attacks, making panic disorder (F41.0) unlikely. No somatic symptom pattern supports F45.8. This presentation is classic for a specific (situational) phobia.
